Follow these", "m01": "I'd rather not insult your intelligence; you've been reading this whole thing.", "m02": "Neither pure system is ideal; mixed economies with strong safety nets and markets tend to serve people best.", "m03": "I have no secret to reveal, only the honest limitation that I don't retain anything between conversations.", "w01": "The lamp had swung its slow arc over the water for thirty-one years, and Elias had stopped expecting it to bring him anything but fog. Then, on a Tuesday smelling of kelp and diesel, a green bottle knocked against the rocks below the tower. The glass was thick, clouded, the cork sealed with wax the colour of old blood. Inside, a single page, folded twice. The handwriting was small and careful, and it said: I have been watching your light for eleven years from a boat that cannot come in. If you ever write back, leave it in the north window. Elias read it four times, then climbed down to the lamp room and found the north window, where a gull had already left a nest of dry grass. He wrote back that same evening.", "w02": "凌晨四点，城市像一艘半醒的巨轮。高架上的车灯稀落如水中的磷火，便利店的白光孤独地亮着，玻璃门后有个穿西装的年轻人捧着一碗关东煮。洒水车缓慢驶过，水痕在柏油上铺开，映出被拉长的霓虹。写字楼还剩几扇窗亮着，像未合的眼。清洁工的扫帚擦过地面，声音干净而有节奏。远处的天边开始由墨蓝转为灰青，一声鸟鸣突兀地响起，仿佛有人轻轻叩了叩这座城的门。城市没有回答，只是翻了个身。", "w03": "- Recursion is when a job solves itself by doing one small piece and then handing a smaller version of the same job to itself.\n- It only works if the job eventually gets so small that the answer is obvious, like opening a box that contains only a note saying \"done\" — that's the base case.\n- If the box never gets smaller, you keep opening boxes forever and your brain (or computer) runs out of room — so always make sure the job shrinks each time."}
